faq.q: What is the origin of Ilaha?
faq.a: Ilaha is associated with Arabic. Ilaha is the Azerbaijani form of Arabic إِلَاهَة (Ilāha), meaning 'goddess, deity'.
Yes — the underlying form إِلَاهَة is Arabic.
Ilaha can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Ilaha should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ilāha is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Ilaha mean in Persian?

faq.a: Romanization variants include Ilaha, ilaha. Script forms are إِلَاهَة, الاهه, الاہہ, الهه, इलाहा.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
